Dhvanyāloka
or Kāvyāloka or Sahṛdayāloka or Sahṛdayahṛdayāloka. alam3k. in 4 sections called Uddyotas; in the form of kārikās an. vṛtti; by Ānandavardhana. [Page311-a.
On the identity of the authors of kārikā an. vṛtti see Kuppuswami Sastri, Upalocana C. on the Locana p. 11; A. Sankaran, The Theories of Rasa an. Dhvani p.. 50-60; Satkar Mookerji, B. C. Law Com. Vol. I. p.. 179-94; K. C. Pandey, Abhinavagupta p.. 202-208; K. Krishnamoorthy, IHQ. 24. p.. 180-94 an. 300-11.
Against the identity see S. K. D., Skt. Poe. 107-116; P. V. Kane, His.. of Skt. Poe. p.. 155 ff.; S. P. Bhattacharya, Proceed. AIOC. VI. p.. 613-22; K. Godavarma, NIA. V. p.. 265-72.
On the origin of the theory of Rasa an. Dhvani see Mukunda Madhava Sarma, The Dhvani Theory in Sanskrit Poetics, Chowk. Skt. Studies 63. 1968; Tapasvi S. Nandi. The Origin an. Development of the Theory of Rasa an. Dhvani in Skt. Poetics. Gujarat University, Ahmedabad, 1973.
